purpose: Incremental investor relations and sponsor-report source evidence for the 762 exact-NCT trial census
scope: Issuer or company IR released clinical efficacy, safety and trial design facts with exact NCT crosswalks; outcomes separate from FDA decisions and trading predictions.

records.specificEvidence: Week 44 clinical remission 25 mg 50.8% and 50 mg 51.3% vs placebo 10.4%; both p<0.0001. Primary endpoint met for both doses.
records.safetyEvidence: Company reports no new safety signal; complete adverse-event tables in release.
records.regulatory: Company intended NDA submission late Q4 2026; not proof of submission or FDA acceptance.
records.crosswalk: Official IR press release identifies ABTECT Maintenance Study 107; registry NCT05535946 sponsor ID ABX464-107

records.specificEvidence: Week 8 clinical remission met for 50 mg and 25 mg versus placebo; placebo-adjusted +19.3% p<0.0001 and +21.4% p<0.0001, respectively.
records.safetyEvidence: Company reports no new safety signals; adverse-event arm table available in release.
records.regulatory: Clinical trial endpoint evidence, not FDA approval.
records.crosswalk: Sponsor Study 105 maps to registry ABX464-105/NCT05507203

records.specificEvidence: Week 8 clinical remission 50 mg primary comparison met (placebo-adjusted +13.4%, p=0.0001). 25 mg comparison not significant (p=0.1034).
records.safetyEvidence: Adverse-event comparison tables in sponsor release.
records.regulatory: Clinical trial endpoint evidence, not FDA approval.

records.safetyEvidence: Issuer reports favorable tolerability and no treatment-related serious adverse events through double-blind phase.
records.regulatory: Company planned NDA submission by end of 2026; not evidence that FDA accepted/approved an application.
records.crosswalk: Issuer's third-quarter 2026 statement explicitly describes LUCIDITY as NCT06747468.

records.safetyEvidence: Company provides trial safety tables; peer-reviewed publication NCT04181723 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02398-1
records.regulatory: Historical phase 3 result; separate drug application/approval date requires application-level match.
records.crosswalk: Peer-reviewed Phase 3 paper explicitly identifies NCT04181723.

records.safetyEvidence: Issuer reports serious adverse events and discontinuation rates for arms.
records.regulatory: Company November 5, 2026 release says sNDA review was extended and reports February 1, 2027 PDUFA date; company statement only, not independent FDA confirmation.
records.crosswalk: Issuer release explicitly cites RISE UP NCT05031780.

records.safetyEvidence: Issuer reports tolerability consistent with earlier studies; per-study safety cannot be inferred from pooled comparison.
records.regulatory: Issuer planned sNDA submission before end of 2026, not independently FDA verified.
records.crosswalk: Arrowhead official issuer release states SHASTA-3 is NCT06347003.

records.specificEvidence: Month 12 median triglyceride reduction versus placebo endpoint met (81% median reduction from baseline, p<0.0001). Pooled acute pancreatitis result applies across SHASTA-3 and -4.
records.safetyEvidence: Issuer reports tolerability consistent with earlier studies; per-study safety cannot be inferred from pooled comparison.
records.regulatory: Issuer planned sNDA submission before end of 2026, not independently FDA verified.
records.crosswalk: Arrowhead official issuer release states SHASTA-4 is NCT06347016.

records.specificEvidence: Sponsor reported both 6- and 12-week continuous abstinence primary comparisons met versus placebo: 25.3% vs 4.4%, and 32.6% vs 7.0%, respectively; both p<0.0001.
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor reported no treatment-related serious adverse events. JAMA 2023 publication PMID 37432430 confirms trial NCT04576949 and reports 6- and 12-week endpoint effects.
records.regulatory: Achieve announced a June 22, 2026 FDA cytisinicline NDA Complete Response Letter citing third-party manufacturing and labeling, with no clinical efficacy or safety deficiencies identified. A regulatory CRL is not a Phase 3 endpoint failure.
records.crosswalk: JAMA 2023 trial publication PMID 37432430 explicitly identifies ORCA-2 as NCT04576949; official sponsor release identifies ORCA-2.

records.specificEvidence: Sponsor reported primary continuous smoking abstinence significantly higher than placebo: 14.8% vs 6.0% for 6-week treatment (p=0.0008), and 30.3% vs 9.4% for 12-week treatment (p<0.0001).
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor reported no treatment-related serious adverse events. JAMA Internal Medicine 2025 trial publication PMID 40257755 independently reports both primary endpoint comparisons.
records.regulatory: Achieve announced a June 22, 2026 FDA cytisinicline NDA Complete Response Letter citing third-party manufacturing and labeling, with no clinical efficacy or safety deficiencies identified. A regulatory CRL is not a Phase 3 endpoint failure.
records.crosswalk: JAMA Internal Medicine 2025 trial publication PMID 40257755 identifies ORCA-3 as NCT05206370; sponsor's May 2023 release identifies ORCA-3.

records.specificEvidence: Sponsor reported adjunctive pimavanserin missed the prespecified full-population primary PANSS total score change at week 6 (p=0.0940). Exploratory/regional positive findings do not change primary endpoint FAIL.
records.safetyEvidence: Company characterized tolerability as consistent with prior studies; this is not a quantitative safety determination.
records.regulatory: The clinical efficacy endpoint was not met in ENHANCE-1. FDA application or PDUFA outcome is not inferred.
records.crosswalk: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02970292 identifies ENHANCE-1 protocol ACP-103-034 (396 participants); sponsor July 22, 2019 release identifies the same 396-person study.

records.specificEvidence: Sponsor reported the week-26 Negative Symptom Assessment-16 primary endpoint did not reach statistical significance: change -11.8 pimavanserin vs -11.1 placebo, p=0.4825. Independent peer-reviewed ADVANCE-2 analysis PMID 40181715 reports P=.48.
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor reported a similar tolerability profile to earlier studies; the peer-reviewed report described 30.4% and 40.3% treatment-emergent adverse-event rates for pimavanserin and placebo, respectively.
records.regulatory: Failed clinical primary endpoint is distinct from any FDA application decision.
records.crosswalk: EudraCT 2019-003343-29 links ADVANCE-2 and protocol ACP-103-064 to NCT04531982; ClinicalTrials.gov protocol for NCT04531982 gives the same study and endpoint.

records.specificEvidence: In the prespecified randomized withdrawal phase, time to psychosis relapse was improved: 12 of 95 (13%) continued pimavanserin vs 28 of 99 (28%) switched to placebo; hazard ratio 0.35 (95% CI 0.17–0.73), two-sided p=0.005. Trial stopped early at prespecified efficacy interim analysis.
records.safetyEvidence: Double-blind adverse events occurred in 41.0% on pimavanserin and 36.6% on placebo. This efficacy result applies to prior responders in the randomized-withdrawal trial, not all dementia patients.
records.regulatory: Prespecified clinical primary endpoint met; not evidence that a dementia-related psychosis label was FDA-approved.
records.crosswalk: NEJM primary report DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2034634 and PMID 34289275 identify HARMONY as NCT03325556.

records.study: ACTIVATE / adult non-regularly transfused PK deficiency
records.specificEvidence: Primary sustained ≥1.5 g/dL hemoglobin response in 40% mitapivat versus 0% placebo (two-sided p<0.0001).
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor described adverse event profile consistent with earlier clinical studies; no independent safety grade has been assigned.
records.regulatory: Prespecified randomized placebo comparison met; FDA approval or PDUFA is a distinct event.
records.crosswalk: ACTIVATE adult non-regular-transfusion study matches NCT03548220; distinguish ACTIVATE-T NCT03559699.
records.regulatoryEvidence: FDA approved mitapivat (PYRUKYND) on Feb 17, 2022 for hemolytic anemia in adults with PK deficiency based on ACTIVATE and ACTIVATE-T. Historical program-level approval; not a prediction for pediatric trials.

records.study: ACTIVATE-T / adult regularly transfused PK deficiency
records.specificEvidence: Ten of 27 adults (37%) achieved ≥33% transfusion burden reduction versus individual historical baseline; one-sided p=0.0002.
records.safetyEvidence: Elevated ALT and headache were each reported in ten participants (37%) in later company safety detail; single-arm study, no placebo AE comparator.
records.regulatory: Historical single-arm efficacy benchmark passed; this is not a randomized placebo comparison or a new FDA approval determination.
records.crosswalk: ACTIVATE-T single-arm 27-person study matches NCT03559699, independently identified in Lancet Haematology PMID 35988546.
records.regulatoryEvidence: FDA approved mitapivat (PYRUKYND) on Feb 17, 2022 for hemolytic anemia in adults with PK deficiency based on ACTIVATE and ACTIVATE-T. Historical program-level approval; not a prediction for pediatric trials.

records.study: ACTIVATE-KidsT (AG348-C-022) / regularly transfused pediatric PK deficiency
records.specificEvidence: Prespecified Bayesian primary statistical criterion was not met with low/moderate adult ACTIVATE-T information borrowing; transfusion reduction responders 9/32 (28.1%) mitapivat versus 2/17 (11.8%) placebo.
records.safetyEvidence: The company described generally well-tolerated treatment and consistency with adult safety data, without an independent grade.
records.regulatory: A numerically favorable response cannot override the prespecified statistical failure.
records.crosswalk: ACTIVATE-KidsT AG348-C-022 is NCT05144256; distinguish nonregular-transfusion ACTIVATE-Kids AG348-C-023.

records.study: ACTIVATE-Kids (AG348-C-023) / nonregularly transfused pediatric PK deficiency
records.specificEvidence: Prespecified Bayesian hemoglobin-response criterion met at all borrowing weights; responders 6/19 (31.6%) mitapivat and 0/11 placebo.
records.safetyEvidence: Issuer reported safety consistent with adult PK deficiency experience; no independent safety grade.
records.regulatory: Pediatric efficacy success does not establish application receipt, review or FDA approval.
records.crosswalk: ACTIVATE-Kids AG348-C-023 maps to NCT05175105, separate from ACTIVATE-KidsT.

records.specificEvidence: Sponsor's pivotal program summary reports week-5 CMAI primary endpoint met in ADVANCE-1 (p=0.010); 15.4-point reduction on AXS-05 versus 11.5 points placebo.
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor's clinical publication describes somnolence, dizziness and diarrhea among treatment-emergent adverse events; not a numerical safety forecast.
records.regulatory: Designated combined Phase 2/3 study in historical Phase 3 census; FDA program decisions must be tracked separately.
records.crosswalk: Peer-reviewed ADVANCE-1 publication maps to NCT03226522; distinguish the separate ADVANCE-2 NCT05557409.
records.regulatoryEvidence: FDA approved AUVELITY (AXS-05, dextromethorphan/bupropion) for agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer disease on Apr 30, 2026 after a priority-review supplemental NDA. This is the overall indication-level regulatory decision across multiple clinical trials; ADVANCE-2 individually failed its primary endpoint.

records.regulatory: Negative trial-specific primary endpoint is not overturned by positive results in other AXS-05 trials.

records.specificEvidence: Week-5 weekly cataplexy attack reduction: 83% AXS-12 versus 66% placebo, p=0.018, primary endpoint met.
records.safetyEvidence: Sponsor lists dry mouth, nausea and constipation as common treatment events; no independent safety grade.
records.regulatory: The 2024 clinical success is distinct from the AXS-12 application/regulatory process.
records.crosswalk: NCT05059223 names SYMPHONY (AXS-12-301), randomized five-week narcolepsy study.
records.regulatoryEvidence: Axsome reported on Nov 2, 2026 that the NDA for AXS-12 (reboxetine), treatment of cataplexy in narcolepsy, is under FDA review; company-reported PDUFA target action date is May 1, 2027. Both SYMPHONY and ENCORE inform the same product-indication application; the date is not a trial-specific FDA decision.

records.specificEvidence: After open-label AXS-12, withdrawal phase week-3 increase in cataplexy attacks was 10.29 per week on placebo versus 1.32 on continuing AXS-12 (p=0.017).
records.safetyEvidence: Company reported no new long-term safety signals in open-label AXS-12 exposure; no independent safety risk grade.
records.regulatory: Responder/exposure-selected randomized withdrawal results, not an all-comers comparator result.
